idiom_name: dumb UIViewController + view model tested by XCTest
implementation_notes: UIKit's form: the view controller stays a dumb view (it forwards actions and renders), while a plain view model owns state and decisions and is exercised by XCTest without a window or a running application; UI automation stays in its own target, which is what keeps the unit suite fast. What replaces the classic humble class is the view model plus a protocol seam for the service, so a fake can be injected; keep the classic controller where the screen is pure layout, and consider Swift Testing for new unit tests where the toolchain supports it.
pitfalls: The view controller creeps back into decisions: IBActions that validate, transform or branch recreate the untestable element; forward raw values and render what the view model publishes.
Lifetime and cycles: a view model that holds the view controller, a delegate or a closure capturing self leaks and makes tests order-dependent.
Async work started in Task keeps running after the screen disappears; cancel on lifecycle events and let tests await expectations instead of sleeping.

variants.name: SwiftUI view + @Observable model (State/Binding)
variants.idiom_name: SwiftUI View + @Observable model wired by State and Binding
variants.implementation_notes: The declarative realization: the View renders from state, the model is an @Observable class (or an ObservableObject) that tests instantiate directly, and State plus Binding wire the two together so SwiftUI updates the interface when data changes. What replaces the classic humble class is the observable model and the framework's automatic updates, which also remove most of the glue a view controller traditionally wrote; choose it for SwiftUI screens, and the UIKit form where the screen is imperative.
pitfalls: The model must be constructible without the view for tests: a model that reads Environment or owns view types only exists inside a SwiftUI hierarchy.
State created inside a view is tied to view identity; inject or create the model once so tests, previews and the running app drive the same object.
